<mxfile host="Electron"> <diagram name="W06 Fixed Camera" id="0"> <mxGraphModel dx="-924" dy="-265" grid="0" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="0" page="0" pageScale="1" pageWidth="1800" pageHeight="1000" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="title" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=18;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#333333;" value="W06 — Fixed-camera shelf intelligence: the Bossa Nova lesson, turned into a design" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="1400" x="40" y="20" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="sub" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=12;fontColor=#666666;" value=""Investment in fixed camera technologies, plus the fast-growing popularity of micro-fulfillment centers, imperils the value proposition of robotic shelf scanning."" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="24" width="1600" x="40" y="54" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="story" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontStyle=1" value="THE STORY THIS PLAN IS BUILT ON

Walmart deployed Bossa Nova shelf-scanning robots in 500+ STORES
from 2017, announced expansion to 1,000, then CANCELLED THE
CONTRACT IN NOVEMBER 2020. Bossa Nova laid off 50% of its staff.

Three years earlier Walmart had called the robots "50% more
productive and three times faster than a human" at inventory-taking.

ALL THREE STATED REASONS WERE NON-TECHNICAL:

1 · LABOUR SUBSTITUTION FLIPPED THE ROI
 the pandemic put more workers in aisles picking for delivery,
 so "they could scan shelves instead of the robots"

2 · CUSTOMER DISCOMFORT
 Walmart US CEO John Furner worried about "how customers
 reacted to the large, SIX-FOOT-TALL MACHINES scanning
 shelves while they shopped"

3 · SIMPLER ALTERNATIVES WON
 "simple and cost-effective ways to manage shelf products
 with workers"

WHAT SURVIVED: floor-cleaning robots that also upload inventory
STAYED in Walmart stores (Brain Corp's niche), and Schnuck Markets
EXPANDED Simbe's Tally to 62 Midwest locations." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="470" width="520" x="40" y="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="cmp" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#cccccc;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=6;verticalAlign=middle;fontStyle=1;" value="COSTS A CAMERA" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="220" x="390" y="300" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="cm2" parent="cmp" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontStyle=1" value="THE HONEST TRADE-OFF
Fixed cameras cost PER BAY. Robots cost PER STORE.

→ so the correct design is SELECTIVE: cameras on the bays where
 out-of-stock costs the most, and NOTHING on the long tail.
 That is a merchandising decision driven by I03 contribution
 data — not a technology decision." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="98" width="600" x="20" y="344" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="arch" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;fontColor=#3d7a2a;" value="Everything below the camera is ALREADY PLANNED" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="470" width="470" x="1290" y="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="a0" parent="arch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontStyle=1" value="shelf-edge + ceiling cameras on SELECTED bays
chosen by lost-sales-per-out-of-stock-hour
(I03 contribution × V03 forecast)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="60" width="430" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="a1" parent="arch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontFamily=Courier New;" value="edge box — the SAME ~$150–300 N100 + OpenVINO from V04
RT-DETRv2 gaps V04
PP-ShiTuV2 which SKU C05
MiniCPM-V on-box verification pass round 2
label read → PROMOTION-ERROR check R01's sleeper feature
occlusion suppression while a person overlaps a bay" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="106" width="430" x="20" y="114" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="a2" parent="arch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="↓ JSON metadata only. No video leaves the store.
MQTT (Mosquitto) → Kafka (Apicurio schema)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="48" width="430" x="20" y="230" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="a3" parent="arch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontFamily=Courier New;" value="stock-service gap → replenishment task, count → reconciliation
I03 planogram compliance deviation → merchandising task
price-service label vs system price → promotion-error task
Grafana on-shelf availability, gap-hours, promo errors" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="86" width="430" x="20" y="288" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="a4" parent="arch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="W06 changes ONLY the sensor placement —
and that single change removes the three reasons
Bossa Nova failed." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="66" width="430" x="20" y="384" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="trust" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fffdf5;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=10;fontStyle=1" value="THE LESSON THAT MATTERS MOST, ENCODED

"Trust is the binding constraint. Solutions must be accurate, actionable and frequent, or vendors lose retailers' and associates' trust — INACCURATE DATA CREATES ADDITIONAL WORK INSTEAD OF FREEING ASSOCIATES UP."

1 · ACTIONABLE, NOT INFORMATIONAL. Never emit "bay 3 looks empty". Emit "replenish SKU-1234 in bay 3, 12 units in the back room, estimated lost sales €48/hour". A task with a quantity and a value, or nothing.
2 · A FALSE POSITIVE COSTS MORE THAN A MISS. An associate walking to a full shelf loses trust permanently. Tune the threshold for PRECISION, not recall, and report precision at the operating point.
3 · MEASURE THE RESPONSE, NOT THE DETECTION. The KPI is GAP-HOURS CLOSED, not gaps found. A detection nobody acts on is worse than no detection, because it cost someone a walk." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="180" width="1720" x="40" y="600" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="priv" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=middle;fontStyle=1" value="PRIVACY — stricter in the EU than the China plan assumed, and CAMERA PLACEMENT IS THE ARGUMENT
No face recognition, no biometric identification (GDPR Art. 9; and biometric categorisation is prohibited-practice territory under the AI Act). No emotion or sentiment inference on customers OR staff — absolute prohibition since Feb 2025. No staff monitoring: declining to build it is the answer.
Cameras point at SHELVES, not aisles. A shelf-edge camera 40cm from a bay, framing the bay, is a fundamentally different privacy proposition from a ceiling camera surveying an aisle — AND IT IS BETTER FOR THE DETECTION TASK. Design and compliance agree here, which is rare and worth saying.
Person detection only for occlusion suppression: box-level, no cross-frame tracking, no identity, discarded immediately. Metadata only leaves the store; SHELF thumbnails retained days not months. DPIA before deployment, signage, lawful basis documented." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="1720" x="40" y="800" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="e1" edge="1" parent="1" source="story" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=3;exitX=1;exitY=0.4;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0;entryY=0.4;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;" target="cmp" value=""> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="e2" edge="1" parent="1" source="cmp" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=3;exitX=1;exitY=0.4;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0;entryY=0.4;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;" target="arch" value=""> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
THE STORY THIS PLAN IS BUILT ON
Walmart deployed Bossa Nova shelf-scanning robots in 500+ STORES
from 2017, announced expansion to 1,000, then CANCELLED THE
CONTRACT IN NOVEMBER 2020. Bossa Nova laid off 50% of its staff.
Three years earlier Walmart had called the robots "50% more
productive and three times faster than a human" at inventory-taking.
ALL THREE STATED REASONS WERE NON-TECHNICAL:
1 · LABOUR SUBSTITUTION FLIPPED THE ROI
the pandemic put more workers in aisles picking for delivery,
so "they could scan shelves instead of the robots"
2 · CUSTOMER DISCOMFORT
Walmart US CEO John Furner worried about "how customers
reacted to the large, SIX-FOOT-TALL MACHINES scanning
shelves while they shopped"
3 · SIMPLER ALTERNATIVES WON
"simple and cost-effective ways to manage shelf products
with workers"
WHAT SURVIVED: floor-cleaning robots that also upload inventory
STAYED in Walmart stores (Brain Corp's niche), and Schnuck Markets
EXPANDED Simbe's Tally to 62 Midwest locations.

div.div:
THE HONEST TRADE-OFF
Fixed cameras cost PER BAY. Robots cost PER STORE.
→ so the correct design is SELECTIVE: cameras on the bays where
out-of-stock costs the most, and NOTHING on the long tail.
That is a merchandising decision driven by I03 contribution
data — not a technology decision.

div.div:
THE LESSON THAT MATTERS MOST, ENCODED
"Trust is the binding constraint. Solutions must be accurate, actionable and frequent, or vendors lose retailers' and associates' trust — INACCURATE DATA CREATES ADDITIONAL WORK INSTEAD OF FREEING ASSOCIATES UP."
1 · ACTIONABLE, NOT INFORMATIONAL. Never emit "bay 3 looks empty". Emit "replenish SKU-1234 in bay 3, 12 units in the back room, estimated lost sales €48/hour". A task with a quantity and a value, or nothing.
2 · A FALSE POSITIVE COSTS MORE THAN A MISS. An associate walking to a full shelf loses trust permanently. Tune the threshold for PRECISION, not recall, and report precision at the operating point.
3 · MEASURE THE RESPONSE, NOT THE DETECTION. The KPI is GAP-HOURS CLOSED, not gaps found. A detection nobody acts on is worse than no detection, because it cost someone a walk.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1706px; height: 1px; padding-top: 855px; margin-left: 14px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
PRIVACY — stricter in the EU than the China plan assumed, and CAMERA PLACEMENT IS THE ARGUMENT
No face recognition, no biometric identification (GDPR Art. 9; and biometric categorisation is prohibited-practice territory under the AI Act). No emotion or sentiment inference on customers OR staff — absolute prohibition since Feb 2025. No staff monitoring: declining to build it is the answer.
Cameras point at SHELVES, not aisles. A shelf-edge camera 40cm from a bay, framing the bay, is a fundamentally different privacy proposition from a ceiling camera surveying an aisle — AND IT IS BETTER FOR THE DETECTION TASK. Design and compliance agree here, which is rare and worth saying.
Person detection only for occlusion suppression: box-level, no cross-frame tracking, no identity, discarded immediately. Metadata only leaves the store; SHELF thumbnails retained days not months. DPIA before deployment, signage, lawful basis documented.
